title: The streets Seattle built over
precision: Public tour meeting address; map marker approximate
summary: After the Great Seattle Fire of 1889, the area was rebuilt with raised street levels, leaving sections of former sidewalks and storefronts below modern streets. Guided tours visit accessible historic passages.
known: Raised streets and surviving underground storefronts are documented by Seattle preservation authorities and tour operators.
unknown: Not all historic underground space is publicly accessible; access varies by property.

title: Port Angeles raised its streets
precision: Tour visitor center; map marker approximate
summary: In 1914, Port Angeles raised downtown streets as a flood-mitigation project, leaving some lower storefronts and passages underneath. A guided heritage tour visits selected spaces.
known: The city street-raising story and surviving accessible passages are described by the heritage tour operator.
unknown: Full historic footprint and boundaries of private remnants are not mapped here.

title: Pendleton under the sidewalks
precision: Public tour meeting address; map marker approximate
summary: The nonprofit Pendleton Underground Tours leads visitors through historic spaces, passageways and business remnants beneath downtown. Its operator explicitly distinguishes documented history from stories preserved through local tradition.
known: Guided public access to historic sub-sidewalk spaces and passageways.
unknown: Not every interpretation or tale on the route is independently verified.

title: Fort Worden coastal batteries
precision: State park general location, not a tunnel entrance
summary: Fort Worden preserves historic gun batteries and military buildings overlooking Admiralty Inlet. It belongs to the coastal defense story, not the later missile-silo program.
known: A Washington State Park with historic fortifications and interpretive features.
unknown: Individual batteries may be closed or restricted depending on conditions.

title: Fort Casey coastal batteries
summary: Historic military gun batteries remain at Fort Casey, now a Washington State Park. Its defensive architecture predates the intercontinental ballistic missile era.
known: Public historic fort with batteries and interpretation.
unknown: Certain structures and interior spaces may not be open.

title: Nike launch area turned park
precision: Modern park location, not an underground feature
summary: This public park occupies the former S-82 Nike missile launch site. The Bainbridge parks plan identifies a former missile assembly building reused as a mini-gym.
known: The former Nike site, its operation period and park reuse are documented.
unknown: No open subterranean route is represented.

title: Nike S-20: Cougar Mountain
precision: Regional park marker, not former launch feature
summary: Nike anti-aircraft installation S-20 operated on Cougar Mountain before its control and launch areas became parkland. Historic missile facilities are largely removed.
known: Deployment period and conversion to public parkland are documented.
unknown: There is no publicly verified underground tour at this location.

title: Titan I: Odessa regional complex
precision: Odessa town center marker ONLY; not the retired complex
summary: One of three Titan I launch complexes associated with Larson Air Force Base. These sites contained deep silos and an interconnected underground support system. Historic sources place this complex in the Odessa vicinity; the pin intentionally indicates only the nearby town.
known: Titan I deployment and retirement in the early 1960s.
unknown: No public access authorized and no precise complex coordinates displayed.

title: Titan I: Warden regional complex
precision: Warden town center marker ONLY; not the retired complex
summary: A Titan I complex in the Warden vicinity formed part of the nine-missile 568th Strategic Missile Squadron. The community-center pin deliberately does not indicate the installation.
known: Historic complex existence, affiliation and retirement date.

title: Titan I: Quincy / Royal City region
precision: Royal City community marker ONLY; not installation
summary: HistoryLink describes the Quincy (Royal City) Titan I complex and notes that it became flooded after decommissioning. It is privately held, closed to visitors, and potentially dangerous.
known: Historic deployment and flooding described in published historical reporting.
unknown: No public entry permitted or mapped here.

title: Atlas E: Reardan regional site
access: Federal research facility; no public entry
precision: Reardan town center ONLY; not the facility
summary: Unlike most Washington missile sites auctioned into private ownership, Atlas E Site 9 near Reardan was retained for federal use and became a research facility. The pin is at the town, not the facility.
known: Site’s historical military use and subsequent federal research use.
unknown: Current facility access unverified; this atlas offers no directions to it.
